p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing the regulatory circuits of the anterior-posterior axis in a Drosophila egg. The top of the structure is labeled, “Translation of mRNA and diffusion of products creates concentration gradients in the embryo.” Below that are four oval-like structures with tails at the top right. The top left side above the structures is labeled Anterior, and the right side is labeled Posterior. The top structure starts off orange (labeled Bicoid), and becomes blue, labeled Nanos. To the left of the Bicoid, the text reads, “Bicoid localized near anterior,” and to the right of the Nanos, the text reads, “Nanos localized near posterior.” A curved, red line, with a dash at the bottom end, points down to the second structure, which starts off orange and turns green. The green end is labeled Caudal. Text to the left of the structure reads, “Bicoid represses Caudal at anterior.” Below that is another structure that starts of gold and becomes dark blue. A red curved arrow points down from the first structure to the gold side of the third structure, and a blue curved line with a dash at the bottom end, points from Nanos to the dark blue side of the third structure. The gold section of the third structure is labeled Hunchback. To the left of this, text reads, “Bicoid activates Hunchback at anterior.” To the right of the dark side, text reads, “Nanos and Pumilio repress Hunchback at posterior.” Below that is a purple structure labeled Pumilio. A line with a dash at the top curves down to Pumilio from the third structure. Below the Pumilio, text reads, “Pumilio is evenly distributed but requires Nanos to repress Hunchback; functions only at posterior.”
